status: provider-boundary implemented; runtime hookup requires source owners

source.predicate: Device::IsHighPerformance rejects SHARP, HTC, and multiplayer-mode source facts; otherwise invokes the selected driver's virtual +0x5c capability method and accepts when result & 0x78 is nonzero.

original_device_predicate_evidence.operation: !SHARP_DEVICES && !HTC_DEVICES && !Is_In_Multiplayer_Mode && ((video_driver->getDriverType() & 0x78) != 0); getDriverType is virtual byte offset 0x5c. This queries the selected driver's identity enum, not an OpenGL feature string or hardware capability probe.

driver_mapping.platform_selection: CAndroidOSDevice::createDriver at 0x6a0454 maps source type 1 to createOpenGLES2Driver and type 0 to createNullDriver; it contains no desktop OpenGL driver branch. The OpenGLES2 constructor delegates to CProgrammableGLDriver and then installs the COpenGLES2 vtable, whose +0x5c override returns 8.
driver_mapping.desktop_opengl_limit: The original ELF symbol inventory records zero COpenGLDriver symbols. Stock Irrlicht 1.6.1 COpenGLDriver::getDriverType returns EDT_OPENGL (value 5), but the local lineage report explicitly says stock COpenGLDriver is not the local backend class. The current custom Windows compatibility renderer therefore has no evidence-backed source driver type 5; WGL/GL_VERSION alone cannot establish it. 5 & 0x78 is zero in any event.
driver_mapping.source_fact_producer: Android front_ui_session_v87.cpp maps exact Build.MANUFACTURER SHARP/HTC and model SHW-M130L into its device facts, while multiplayer_mode is explicitly initialized to zero at bind. Windows currently has no matching source Build/global-fact owner. IsHighPerformance consumes sharp, htc, and multiplayer_mode; no_igp is consumed earlier by NativeIsMultiplayerEnabled, not by this predicate.

game_object_init_post_consumer.original_function: GameObject::InitPost at 0x38be5c; ObjectBase::InitPost then CheckSpawnProbability precede the device call. Device is queried only for an accepted spawn whose VisualObject +0x2d8 is null.
game_object_init_post_consumer.observable_branch: If the host's quality result is low and source byte +0x60 (facultative) and source byte +0x10c are both nonzero, InitPost leaves the visual pointer null and skips LoadVisualObject. Otherwise it calls LoadVisualObject and Sync only if a visual is then present. This branch changes optional visual loading only; it does not change spawn probability, eligibility, transforms, AABB, or PF registration.
game_object_init_post_consumer.field_evidence: GameObject::DeclareProperties at 0x38cee8 registers `facultative` at +0x60 with default true. The +0x10c byte is read by InitPost but has no recovered property name; retain it as an unknown source flag.
game_object_init_post_consumer.policy_recommendation: For the in-house Windows port, the GameObjectInitializationServicesV1.device_high_performance callback may honestly report the actual Renderer/App visual-quality policy. Validate the same current WGL context and retained Renderer owner first, then ask the owner's explicit selected profile/capability provider (for example, full source-visual loading only where the current renderer supports it). This is a port policy mapping, not a recovered original COpenGLDriver or an Android driver enum. Fail if context, renderer owner, or policy is unavailable. Keep SHARP/HTC/multiplayer source precedence only when those actual application facts are supplied; NO_IGP is not used by GameObject::InitPost.

implementation.in_house_game_object_policy: GameObjectVisualQualityWglV1 is the behavior-equivalent Windows path. Bind it to the actual current WGL context when the renderer starts. Each GameObjectInitializationServicesV1.device_high_performance callback rechecks the same HDC/HGLRC/thread, then asks a retained Renderer/App policy provider for the selected visual-quality result. The Renderer/App provider owns the quality profile and any capability evidence; this type claims no original Driver::getDriverType identity.
implementation.wgl_witness: Reads actual wglGetCurrentContext(), wglGetCurrentDC(), and GetCurrentThreadId(); binds and validates their identity and the real ContextResourceBudgetV37 lease/generation.
implementation.inputs: Requires injected actual budget lease, actual source MenuDeviceFactsV1 provider, and actual selected source driver's virtual +0x5c capability provider. No WGL context is translated into Android GLES facts or a guessed source capability value.
implementation.lifetime: Provider owns only a weak lease to the selected shared budget and a bound context/thread witness. Caller owns the WGL context, budget, source driver, and fact providers. Call context_lost when the selected context is destroyed or replaced.

integration_limit: The current Windows-foundation renderer owns a compatibility WGL context but no source Device object, source device-fact provider, or ContextResourceBudgetV37. The original source-driver predicate therefore remains unavailable. For GameObject::InitPost in the in-house port, a separately named/owned Renderer/App visual-quality policy can satisfy its observable optional-visual gate without claiming original-driver identity; validate actual current WGL ownership and make missing context, renderer, or policy an explicit failure. The budget API has no native HGLRC field: construct one shared ContextResourceBudgetV37, call begin_context with the selected WGL context current, share that same lease with every actual GPU owner and this provider, and call context_lost before context teardown/replacement. The current Renderer does not route GL textures through the budget, so an empty ready ledger alone is not an actual resource-budget owner.

validation.result: Provider and GameObjectVisualQualityWglV1 compiled and linked against the native Windows API, original source predicate, and real ContextResourceBudgetV37 implementation. The existing resource-budget source emits one misleading-indentation warning; provider code compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -Werror by itself.
validation.runtime: No runtime source-driver result is claimed; current Windows-foundation does not own a source Device or actual ContextResourceBudgetV37 lease.
